run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: No root cause can be tied to this alert from the data reachable in this Run. The two supplied Elasticsearch indices exist and contain only ci-cd-cluster records: in the authorized window 2026-11-21T12:57:00Z–2026-11-22T12:57:00Z, app-235-change-history holds 3 changes, all cluster=ci-cd, namespace=ci (jenkins 2.426.2-lts→2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-22T06:56:47Z, argocd-server v2.9.2→v2.9.3 at 07:56:47Z, gitlab-runner scaled 2→3 at 10:56:47Z), and its newest record is 10:56:47Z, roughly 1.5 h before the alert's implied start (~12:27Z). The inventory holds the same three apps, all status Running. Neither index contains any record for app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, cluster us-prod-eks, or org clientorg-alpha, and the connected Kubernetes cluster is a single kind node opspilot-m1-control-plane running otel-demo (no ci namespace, no jenkins/argocd/gitlab-runner workloads). Its Prometheus alerting-rules ConfigMap defines only CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh and two OpsPilot self alerts, labelled cluster=opspilot-m1, not onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease. In the connected cluster all 24 deployments report ready==available, all 32 pods are Running/ready with start times on 2026-11-20, every ReplicaSet was created 2026-11-20 (no rollout in the window), the node is Ready without pressure, no Ingress exists, and every fault-injection flag in the flagd ConfigMap has defaultVariant=off. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for every query attempted, so application error-rate and latency signals for the incident were not checked. The main finding is therefore a scope mismatch: the alert's environment is not the environment the available sources describe, and the 'started right after a deployment' premise is not supported by the change history, whose latest entry is 1.5 h earlier and concerns a CI runner replica scale.

claims.text: Both supplied indices exist: app-235-cluster-inventory (4 documents) and app-235-change-history (4 documents), both green/open at query time.

In app-235-change-history inside the window there are exactly 3 records, all cluster=ci-cd and namespace=ci: deployment BUILD-7X4Q9M for jenkins (2.426.2-lts→2.426.3-lts, changed_by infra-team, 2026-11-22T06:56:47Z), deployment BUILD-3NR8Y1 for argocd-server (v2.9.2→v2.9.3, 2026-11-22T07:56:47Z), and scale BUILD-5PW2K6 for gitlab-runner (2→3 replicas, v16.7.0, 2026-11-22T10:56:47Z).

The newest change record in the window is timestamp 2026-11-22T10:56:47Z (oldest 06:56:47Z); change_type buckets are deployment=2 and scale=1, app_name buckets are argocd-server=1, gitlab-runner=1, jenkins=1, and the only cluster bucket is ci-cd.

app-235-cluster-inventory inside the window contains 3 documents, with app_name buckets argocd-server=1, gitlab-runner=1, jenkins=1, the only cluster bucket ci-cd, the only namespace bucket ci, and the only status bucket Running (replicas 1, 2 and 3 respectively).

No record in either index within the window carries the alert's app_name lambda-dashboard-monitoring, cluster us-prod-eks or org clientorg-alpha; the aggregation over app-235-cluster-inventory returns only the ci-cd cluster, ci namespace and the three apps, and app-235-change-history returns only the ci-cd cluster bucket.
The connected Kubernetes cluster has namespaces default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo — there is no namespace named ci.

The connected cluster's 24 deployments are all in kube-system, local-path-storage or otel-demo (coredns, metrics-server, local-path-provisioner, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart); each reports available replicas equal to desired replicas, and no jenkins, argocd-server or gitlab-runner deployment exists.

All 32 pods in the connected cluster are phase Running and their containers report ready=true; the otel-demo application pods have startTime 2026-11-20T16:32–16:33Z (no pod started during the incident window), while etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler pods on opspilot-m1-control-plane have startTime 2026-11-22T08:04:14Z.
All 26 ReplicaSets in the cluster have creationTimestamp 2026-11-20 (16:31–16:33Z); none was created during the authorized window, so no rollout occurred in the window.

The otel-demo flagd ConfigMap demo.flagd.json defines fault flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has defaultVariant "off" (state ENABLED).

The flagd pod logged only its startup banner and service-listener lines at 2026-11-22T08:04:21Z (version v0.12.8, listening on 8013/8014/8015/8016, watching ./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json); no flag-change or configuration-reload line appears in the window.

The Prometheus ConfigMap alerting_rules.yml in this cluster defines only CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (error ratio of checkout CheckoutService/PlaceOrder server spans > 0.5 for 2m, labels cluster=opspilot-m1) and the OpsPilot self alerts OpsPilotAgentAbsent and OpsPilotModelCallsFailing; it contains no rule named onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease and no rule referencing lambda-dashboard-monitoring or clientorg-alpha.
The cluster has a single node opspilot-m1-control-plane (kubelet v1.37.0, Debian GNU/Linux 13) with Ready=True and MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False.
No Ingress object exists in the cluster (the ingress list is empty).

Against a deployment-triggered failure in the reachable environment: every deployment reports ready==available replicas, every ReplicaSet predates the window by more than a day, and the newest recorded change anywhere in the supplied indices is 2026-11-22T10:56:47Z (a gitlab-runner replica scale in cluster ci-cd), roughly 1.5 h before the alert's implied ~12:27Z start.

Against this cluster being the alert's origin: the only alert rules loaded here are labelled cluster=opspilot-m1 and cover checkout PlaceOrder error ratio plus OpsPilot self-monitoring, whereas the alert payload names app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, cluster us-prod-eks and grafana_dashboard_name Production-Performance-Overview.

The alert most likely originates from an environment (us-prod-eks / clientorg-alpha, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring) that is not represented in any of the reachable sources, so its triggering change cannot be identified here; the ci-cd inventory/change indices and the connected otel-demo kind cluster describe different estate.

If the failing workload is in the ci-cd estate, the only change near the alert is the gitlab-runner replica scale at 2026-11-22T10:56:47Z; whether it relates to an online-device count decline is unverified, because no device, lambda-dashboard or monitoring signal exists in the accessible sources.

Rejected: the jenkins LTS bump 2.426.2-lts→2.426.3-lts (BUILD-7X4Q9M, 2026-11-22T06:56:47Z) as the trigger — it is ~5.5 h before the alert, belongs to a different app/namespace/cluster than the alert payload, and no error or impact evidence for jenkins was observed.

Rejected: the argocd-server security patch v2.9.2→v2.9.3 (BUILD-3NR8Y1, 2026-11-22T07:56:47Z) as the trigger — it precedes the alert by ~4.5 h, targets a different service than the alert payload, and the inventory still lists argocd-server as Running with 2 replicas.

Rejected as a fault-injection cause inside the reachable cluster: all fault flags in the flagd ConfigMap (productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, kafkaQueueProblems, recommendationCacheFailure) are set to defaultVariant "off", and flagd logged no flag change in the window.

Obtain the inventory and change records for cluster us-prod-eks / org clientorg-alpha (the estate the alert actually names), including any Grafana/lambda-dashboard-monitoring deployment in the hours before the alert, since neither supplied index covers it.

Restore or authorize read access to the Prometheus and Jaeger endpoints and re-run error-rate and latency checks (for example error ratio of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"} and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count by rpc_grpc_status_code), which were unreachable in this Run.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for every query type attempted (list_prometheus_rules, get_metric_names, get_all_labels, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query) — all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE — so no error-rate, latency, grpc status-code or kube-state-metrics reading for the incident window (including traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) could be checked; a missing series is unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services and traces_search on checkout both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span, status or error-detail evidence exists for any service.
The change_history integration is listed as not_integrated; only the app-235-change-history Elasticsearch index was available, and it covers the ci-cd cluster only.

Each index reports 4 documents but only 3 fall inside the authorized window and the time filter cannot be disabled, so the 4th document in app-235-change-history and in app-235-cluster-inventory is unread and unknown; it could name another app or cluster.

No Kubernetes events were returned for the authorized window (the grouped all-namespace events query matched nothing), so event-based evidence such as Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy or rollout events is unknown.

Error-pattern log queries against checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n, cart-549b8757d-zjgcd, payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and product-catalog-777f5468d4-hc8rj returned no matching lines with status no_data, and frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw returned zero log bytes; these results show only that the queries matched nothing and cannot establish those services' health.

The etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler pods on opspilot-m1-control-plane have startTime 2026-11-22T08:04:14Z, i.e. they changed during the window; no evidence shows what caused that restart or ties it to the alert.
The alert's startsAt is a relative description ("30 minutes ago") without an absolute timestamp, so the alert start (~2026-11-22T12:27Z) is inferred from the run time rather than observed.

No signal of any kind for onlineDevices count, lambda-dashboard-monitoring, org clientorg-alpha or cluster us-prod-eks exists in the reachable sources; the metric and label names that could show it (e.g. an app_* online-devices counter) could not be enumerated because Prometheus was unreachable.
next_steps: Ask the alerting environment owner for the us-prod-eks / clientorg-alpha change records around 2026-11-22T11:30–12:30Z, since the supplied indices contain only ci-cd entries.

Confirm whether this alert was routed to the wrong cluster/team and whether an online-devices metric (and its Grafana dashboard Production-Performance-Overview) is scraped by a Prometheus this Run cannot reach.

If impact in ci-cd is suspected, verify with its owners whether the gitlab-runner scale 2→3 at 2026-11-22T10:56:47Z and the argocd-server patch to v2.9.3 at 07:56:47Z were intentional and whether runner registration or job throughput changed afterwards.
Re-run the Prometheus and Jaeger checks once those endpoints are reachable to test whether any otel-demo service shows a real error-rate or latency deviation in the window.

content:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
